items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: After Bob Strong I went with Jan Savitt’s Orchestra, who was kind of a pretty well named band of the 40’s.

ctx.x: That was about the way I really got into it I guess. And playing around Mobile for a couple of years, I think I was about 16. There was a band from Auburn, Alabama, they were known as the Auburn Knights, a college band, a very good big band, and they were playing a date in Mobile and they came up to this place called the Airport Restaurant where I was playing with a little band, and they heard me play and they offered me a chance to go up to Auburn and play with their band, although I was still in high school. So…

it was. So we went up there and a big band came through there that was looking for a trombone player, and so this was in the summertime, a band by the name of Tommy Reynolds, and he was from New York. He was one of the up-and-coming new bands and they were going into the Lincoln Hotel in New York I think, but I couldn’t say, because I had to go back in finish high school. But anyway, I met a lot of guys that I ran into later on in life. One of them in particular, a fellow named Al Ramsey was a trumpet player who…
By this time was music your career? I mean you said okay, I’m going to be a musician now. This is something I can do.
